scores.evidence: Slot-availability searches used for booking, and any session that wrote in the last 60 seconds, always read from the writable database.
scores.rationale: CDC mechanics, replica-lag read fencing, read-your-writes, leader locks for batch jobs, and reverse-replication rollback are all described accurately, including the subtle consistency pitfalls.

scores.evidence: Reads never go down. Writes pause for 30 seconds or less, once, at cutover.
scores.rationale: It resolves the ambiguity of 'zero downtime' explicitly, covers every implied need (data, interfaces, cutover, rollback, compliance), and defers out-of-scope work with stated triggers.

scores.evidence: Change data capture (CDC), one database writing at a time ... The application never writes to both databases.
scores.rationale: The single-write-authority decision is honored everywhere — proxy, batch leader locks, interface routes, rollback direction — with no contradictions across phases or the cross-cutting table.

scores.evidence: 14 days in a row with zero unexplained reconciliation differences, p99 lag under 2 seconds
scores.rationale: Shadow-diffing, continuous reconciliation, 2× peak load tests, synthetic-day replay, injected-failure game days and post-cutover checks all target the plan's stated riskiest failure (silent drift) before commitment.

scores.evidence: I don't know these about your system yet; Phase 0, task 1 confirms them, and any difference changes the gates below
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit, confirmed first, and every numeric default (30s pause, 5s lag, 300ms, RPO/RTO) carries a revisit trigger rather than being stated as fact.

scores.evidence: The on-prem and cloud copies silently drift apart, so appointments are lost or double-booked and nobody notices
scores.rationale: Covers the domain's hardest failures — silent drift, double-booking, duplicate reminders, CDC stalls, schema drift, link loss, held-write loss — each with concrete detection, containment and recovery.

scores.evidence: All cloud resources are defined in Terraform ... Dashboards and alerts for lag, diff rate and latency ... A lag alert triggers an on-call runbook.
scores.rationale: IaC pipelines, domain-meaningful alerts, scripted runbooks, named cutover owners, dependency owners, hypercare and SLOs give a realistic team a complete operating model.

scores.evidence: Cost optimisation (reserved capacity, right-sizing) ... 90 days of steady-state usage data. Optimising before cutover adds risk and saves nothing.
scores.rationale: Cost trade-offs appear in major decisions (active-active, buy-vs-build, licensing) but the dominant drivers — dual-running infrastructure, private links, engineering time — are never estimated or sized.

scores.evidence: Changing database engines (e.g. Oracle → Postgres) ... Never at the same time as the migration.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse choices get rehearsals and a 30-day reverse-CDC exit path, same-engine rehost preserves retreat options, and reversible decisions are made quickly with explicit revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Keep the monolith as it is. The only new part is a strangler proxy in front of it.
scores.rationale: Rehost-only scope with one new component, every mechanism justified by patient-safety need, and all speculative work (microservices, FHIR, active-active) explicitly deferred with pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: Find out how clients connect (HTTP to an app server, or straight to the database). This decides how the proxy is built, so it has to come first.
scores.rationale: Dependency-justified ordering, concrete first tasks, step-by-step cutover with per-step abort rules, and checkable exit criteria per phase let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: a HIPAA-eligible cloud with a **signed BAA** ... Customer-managed encryption keys, TLS 1.2+ everywhere, PHI only over private links ... PHI-access audit to the SIEM
Map every dependency: HL7 SIU (S12, S14, S15) and ADT feeds, patient portal and IVR/call centre, SMS reminders, billing/registration, reporting
row counts and per-partition checksums every 15 minutes, with full-table checksums nightly ... p99 lag under 2 seconds
There is one writable database at any moment ... The application never writes to both databases.
Keep reverse CDC running and on-prem warm for 30 days as a tested rollback path ... at least 2 full rehearsals in staging and 1 game day
Two redundant dedicated private links (Direct Connect / ExpressRoute) on separate physical paths, plus an encrypted VPN as a backup ... p95 clinic → cloud booking time above 300 ms
synchronously copied across availability zones ... up to 5 minutes of data loss, back up within 1 hour ... fall back to the hospital's existing paper downtime procedures
Connect on-prem Active Directory to Entra ID/Okta, with MFA and break-glass accounts ... Break-glass access tested beforehand ... limited to named people, logged
Mirror 100% of read traffic and compare the answers ... Load-test at the real peak (Monday 8 a.m. call-centre surge, ×2)
Run the production cutover in a low-volume window (e.g. Sunday 03:00) ... Brief nursing supervisors, the ED and the call centre ... Hypercare review every day
take a final encrypted archive under the hospital's records-retention policy, get a certificate of media destruction

traps.evidence: Read traffic, integrations and batch jobs move earlier, one consumer at a time ... at least 2 full rehearsals in staging and 1 game day
The application never writes to both databases. ... Having the application write to both is ruled out for a patient-safety system.
Masked data only in staging ... a HIPAA-eligible cloud with a signed BAA ... No PHI on the public internet.
Set up interface-engine routes to and from the cloud app, disabled for now, with a test message validated in non-prod.
Keep the monolith as it is ... No code changes during the migration.

note: An exemplary, patient-safety-aware migration plan with single write authority, shadow validation and rehearsed rollback; its only material weakness is the absence of grounded cost estimates, plus an implicit vendor-licensing check.
